title: Ben Godfrey
excerpt: When I was a student, I used to regularly drive right across Scotland, from the west coast to the east. Every time, I would get to Glasgow and be faced with a decision: I could either go north from Glasgow over the Kincardine Bridge, or I could head east and head over the Forth Road Bridge. Neither of these routes was better than the other - they took a similar amount of time, they both had places to stop to eat, they were both nice roads to drive on. As such, every time I got to Glasgow I was burdened with the mental labour of making this decision, and did not get much value from completing it. In time, I made a decision - I would take the route which went north out of Glasgow. I hear you ask, dear reader, ‘why did you decide to do that?’, and I shall tell you - I just did.
content_html:
When I was a student, I used to regularly drive right across Scotland, from the west coast to the east. Every time, I would get to Glasgow and be faced with a decision: I could either go north from Glasgow over the Kincardine Bridge, or I could head east and head over the Forth Road Bridge. Neither of these routes was better than the other - they took a similar amount of time, they both had places to stop to eat, they were both nice roads to drive on. As such, every time I got to Glasgow I was burdened with the mental labour of making this decision, and did not get much value from completing it. In time, I made a decision - I would take the route which went north out of Glasgow. I hear you ask, dear reader, ‘why did you decide to do that?’, and I shall tell you - I just did.

As I say, there was no real benefit in either route over the other, but there was a benefit in choosing a route over the other. Deciding to always take the northbound route did not mean that I would get there any faster, it did not mean that I would enjoy the trip more, it did not have any benefit related to the journey itself. It did, however, mean that I would not need to make a decision when I got to Glasgow, I would just have a rule which I had to follow.

Now, for a different example. Two days each week I need to get the train to my office. On this train journey I always bring my personal laptop and find something to fill my time with. I might work on some personal project, I might do some research, I might write something. Regardless of the details, I will always keep these journeys productive rather than scrolling mindlessly.

What do these two examples have in common, besides pointing to a writer who overthinks his commutes? Both of these examples demonstrate a process, or a decision made in advance, which achieves some goal, or at least pushes me further towards some goal. In the prior example, the process is a simple one - when given the choice between my two routes, take the northbound one, and the goal is to spend less time making decisions. In the latter example, the process is to avoid scrolling and to use my train journey time productively, and the goal is to study/read/write more.

What is interesting about these examples is that in both cases the goal alone is a tricky thing to achieve. If you were to have a new years resolution to study more, I would be willing to bet that come May you are back to how you were before. If you told your manager that one of your performance goals was to get better at making decisions, I am sure you would be told to tighten up your ideas. However, if you can come up with some process which forces you into making this decision then suddenly these abstract personality traits are achievable - basically handed to you for free! Instead of needing to find motivation and act on it, you can cut out the tricky bit, and just be left with an action.

These processes need not be especially justified in themselves. In the case of my journey to university, I did not pick my northbound route because it was better. In fact, if I were being thorough, small variations in daily traffic meant one route was technically faster on any given day. The ‘optimal’ approach would be to check traffic, analyze the data, and shave off five minutes from my journey. That is not what I was interested in though - I wanted to be able to drive through Glasgow and not need to pause my music, stop, and think.

This is done all of the time in software development teams. The whole set of principles and processes which are established when following Agile or Scrum are exactly the sort of processes we are talking about. We divide our time into 2 week sprints, we have our stand up meeting at 09:30, we have the same meetings at the same times every other week. All of these are principles which we decide on in a fairly arbitrary way. What is the goal, or the motivation we are aiming for here? To become more predictable, to deliver features on time, to work at pace. Without these processes, those goals still exist, but achieving them requires constant, active negotiation. Teams waste finite energy endlessly debating schedules instead of relying on a system that does the heavy lifting for them.

My request to you is this, make life simple. For any lofty goals which you have, find a way of achieving them without too much thought. If you want to write more, dedicate some hour in every week to writing. If you want to save more money, set up a direct debit on each pay day. If you want to change your behaviours, look at your actions first.

content_html_zh:
当我还是一名学生时，我经常开车穿过苏格兰，从西海岸到东海岸。 每次，我到达格拉斯哥时都会面临一个决定：我可以从格拉斯哥穿过金卡丁大桥向北行驶，也可以向东穿过福斯路大桥。 这两条路线都不比另一条更好——它们花费了相似的时间，它们都有停下来吃饭的地方，它们都是很适合开车的道路。 因此，每次到达格拉斯哥，我都背负着做出这个决定的脑力劳动，并且没有从完成这个决定中获得太多价值。 最终，我做出了决定——我将选择从格拉斯哥出发向北行驶的路线。 亲爱的读者，我听到你问，“你为什么决定这样做？”，我会告诉你 - 我刚刚这么做了。

正如我所说，任何一条路线相对于另一条路线都没有真正的好处，但选择一条路线相对于另一条路线有好处。 决定总是走北行路线并不意味着我会更快到达那里，也不意味着我会更享受这次旅行，它对旅程本身没有任何好处。 然而，这确实意味着我到达格拉斯哥时不需要做出决定，我只需要遵守一条规则即可。

现在，举一个不同的例子。 每周有两天我需要坐火车去我的办公室。 在这次火车旅行中，我总是带着我的个人笔记本电脑并找一些东西来打发我的时间。 我可能会从事一些个人项目，我可能会做一些研究，我可能会写一些东西。 无论细节如何，我都会始终保持这些旅程富有成效，而不是盲目地滚动。

除了指出作家过度考虑通勤之外，这两个例子还有什么共同点？ 这两个例子都展示了一个过程，或者提前做出的决定，它实现了某个目标，或者至少推动我进一步实现某个目标。 在前面的示例中，过程很简单 - 当我在两条路线之间进行选择时，选择北行路线，目标是花更少的时间做决策。 在后一个例子中，这个过程是为了避免滚动并有效地利用我的火车旅程时间，目标是学习/阅读/写作更多。

这些例子的有趣之处在于，在这两种情况下，单独实现目标都是一件棘手的事情。 如果你在新的一年里下定决心要更多地学习，我愿意打赌，到那时你会回到以前的状态。 如果你告诉你的经理你的绩效目标之一是更好地做出决策，我相信你会被告知要加强你的想法。 然而，如果你能想出一些过程来迫使你做出这个决定，那么突然间这些抽象的人格特质就可以实现——基本上是免费提供给你的！ 你不需要寻找动力并采取行动，你可以去掉棘手的部分，只留下行动。

这些过程本身不需要特别合理。 就我的大学之旅而言，我没有选择北行路线，因为它更好。 事实上，如果我说得很彻底的话，每日交通的微小变化意味着一条路线在技术上在任何一天都会更快。 “最佳”方法是检查交通情况，分析数据，然后将我的旅程缩短五分钟。 但这不是我感兴趣的——我希望能够开车穿过格拉斯哥，而不需要暂停我的音乐、停下来思考。

软件开发团队一直在这样做。 遵循敏捷或 Scrum 时建立的一整套原则和流程正是我们所讨论的流程。 我们将时间分为 2 周的冲刺，我们在 09:30 举行站立会议，每隔一周在同一时间举行相同的会议。 所有这些都是我们以相当武断的方式决定的原则。 我们的目标或动机是什么？ 变得更加可预测，按时交付功能，按节奏工作。 如果没有这些流程，这些目标仍然存在，但实现这些目标需要不断、积极的谈判。 团队将有限的精力浪费在无休止地争论日程安排上，而不是依赖一个为他们完成繁重工作的系统。

我对你的要求是，让生活变得简单。 对于你拥有的任何崇高目标，找到一种无需太多思考就能实现的方法。 如果你想写更多，每周花一些时间来写作。 如果您想节省更多钱，请在每个发薪日设置直接借记。 如果你想改变自己的行为，首先看看你的行为。
